_comment: Type-checks the test files, which tsconfig.json deliberately excludes.
WHY THEY ARE EXCLUDED THERE: several tests cover the Expo app, whose
pure logic has no runner of its own, by importing files under
eddy-ios/. That pulled mobile source into `next build`s type-check, and
Vercel installs only missouri-float-planner/ — so @eddy/types, which
resolves locally through eddy-ios/node_modules, was not resolvable
there and broke the deploy. The web production build has no business
type-checking tests, and now does not.
WHY THE PATH ALIASES ARE HERE: they let these tests resolve the shared
Eddy packages from source directly, so CI does not need the Expo app
installed to check them.
AND THE TEST RUNNER MUST BE POINTED AT THIS FILE, which is the half that
was missing. `npm test` runs tsx, and tsx reads ./tsconfig.json unless it
is told otherwise — so the aliases above governed `tsc` and nothing else.
At runtime @eddy/types fell back to ordinary node resolution, which walks
up from eddy-ios/src/lib/ and finds eddy-ios/node_modules/@eddy/types on
any machine where the Expo app has been installed. Every laptop. Not the
lint-and-typecheck job, which runs `npm ci` in missouri-float-planner
only — so first-run-rivers.test.ts died on MODULE_NOT_FOUND there and
passed everywhere a human would look. The script now runs
`tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.test.json`; see package.json.
Only VALUE imports are affected, which is why this took a while to fire:
tsx erases `import type`, so a test could import a dozen types from
@eddy/types and never notice. riverDistance.ts imports hasCoordinates,
which is a function.
It is a SUPERSET of the build config rather than tests-only: replacing
`include` dropped Next's ambient type augmentations (RequestInit.next and
friends), which every route file depends on. Checking everything here is
also what tsc --noEmit did before the split, so CI coverage is unchanged.
